title: A Uniform for the Typewriter
premise: In 1911, Theo Blackwood, a pearl diver's son indentured to the Meridian Trading Company, works as a clerk in a coastal workshop where ledgers are typed and secrets are filed. When a census taker's probing questions expose that Theo has been quietly forging records to hide the company's exploitation of dying divers, he learns his late father left him a hidden ledger proving everything. To publish it, Theo must finish typing the evidence before the company burns the workshop and its archives; he succeeds at terrible cost, losing his anonymity and nearly his life, but the truth survives in print.
about_author: Ivo Vane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing colonial trade records in Southeast Asia. Their fiction excavates the quiet rebellions buried in bureaucratic paper.

chapters.title: The Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A census taker visits the Meridian workshop and asks about families of deceased divers, forcing Theo to lie while typing the falsified death rolls himself. That night he finds his father's name on a list marked 'settled'—paid off and forgotten. The emotional beat is dread: invisibility, Theo realizes, was always someone else's arrangement, not his own achievement.

chapters.title: What the Diver Left
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, with flashbacks to his father. Following a pearl shell etched with coordinates, Theo finds a waterproof satchel beneath the old diving jetty containing his father's true accounts—diver deaths, withheld wages, bribed officials. He begins secretly retyping them at night. The emotional beat is inheritance: grief transmuted into purpose, and the first taste of dangerous hope.

chapters.title: Ash Before Ink
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Theo and the workshop manager, Crane, who suspects a leak and orders the archives burned. Theo races to finish the final pages as smoke fills the building, hiding the manuscript inside a typewriter case while Crane confronts him. The climax: beaten and interrogated, Theo refuses to confess, betting everything that the pages already left the building in a mail sack.

chapters.title: A Uniform for the Typewriter
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, weeks later. The ledger reaches a newspaper; investigations begin, Crane is arrested, and Theo—no longer invisible—is summoned to testify under his own name for the first time. He keeps the scorched typewriter as his only inheritance. The emotional beat is bittersweet resolution: survival cost him his father's silence, but gave him a voice, and the price was worth paying.
